name: Kansas City Lowball
description: Kansas City Lowball (also known as Deuce-to-Seven Lowball) is a prestigious poker variant where the *worst* traditional poker hand wins. It uses 'Deuce-to-Seven' ranking: Aces are high and undesirable, and straights and flushes are counted against the player. The goal is to make the lowest possible five-card hand that is not a straight or flush. It is renowned for being the 'purist's lowball' and is a staple of the World Series of Poker.

overview.description: Kansas City Lowball (also known as Deuce-to-Seven Lowball) is a prestigious poker variant where the *worst* traditional poker hand wins. It uses 'Deuce-to-Seven' ranking: Aces are high and undesirable, and straights and flushes are counted against the player. history.origins: Developed in the mid-20th century in the poker rooms of Kansas City and later Las Vegas. It was designed to provide a more difficult strategic challenge than 'California Lowball' (Ace-to-Five).
timeline: 1950s: Emerges as a high-stakes professional game.
1970s: Included in the World Series of Poker (WSOP) as a $10,000 championship event.
1990s: Popularity spikes among high-stakes 'Mixed Game' players.
Present: Remains the standard for high-stakes lowball poker worldwide.
history.cultural: Often called 'The Great Game' by professionals due to the intense psychological pressure and the high value of 'snowshoeing' (bluffing with a bad hand).
history.evolution: The transition from 'Single Draw' (one chance to exchange) to 'Triple Draw' (three chances) in modern years has added layers of betting and complexity.

setup.players: Up to 7 players. Played with Blinds (Small and Big).
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 5 cards face down. In Single Draw, there is one exchange phase; in Triple Draw, there are three.
setup.equipment: Standard cards, poker chips, dealer button.

rules.objective: Have the 'lowest' hand at the showdown, where straights and flushes are considered high (bad).
rules.gameplay: 1. Players receive 5 cards. 2. First betting round. 3. Draw phase: Players discard any number of cards and receive replacements. 4. Second betting round (Check/Bet/Raise/Fold). 5. (In Triple Draw, repeat steps 3-4 twice more). 6. **Showdown**: Lowest hand wins the pot.
keyRules: Hand rankings are inverted: worst poker hand wins
Aces are always HIGH (above King) - very bad for low
Straights and flushes count as high hands - avoid them
Best possible hand: 7-5-4-3-2 (unsuited) - 'The Wheel' or 'Number One'
Pairs, trips, quads are very bad hands
Blinds: Small Blind and Big Blind start the action
No qualifier needed - any five cards can win

strategy.basic: Do not draw to a straight or flush. If you have 3-4-5-6, drawing a 2 or 7 will GIVE you a straight, which is essentially a losing hand. Aim for 'disconnected' low cards like 2-3-5-7.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Smooth' hand: A 9-7-6-4-2 is 'smooth' because it is much lower than a 9-8-7-6-2. 'Smoothness' refers to how low your second and third cards are.
strategy.advanced: Snowing: A powerful bluff where you stand pat (don't draw any cards) despite having a pair or a high card. If you act confident, players with legitimate 9s or 10s may fold, thinking you have a 7 or 8.
tips: In Single Draw, don't enter the pot unless you can draw just 1 or 2 cards to a 9-low or better.
The Deuce (2) is the most important card in your hand. Without it, your hand is significantly more vulnerable to being out-lowed.
